items.title: Added /config key=value syntax to set any setting from the prompt (e.g. /config thinking=false) — works in interactive, -p, and Remote Control

explanation.what_it_is: The /config key=value syntax allows you to set any Claude Code setting directly from the prompt. This syntax can be used in interactive mode, with the -p flag, or in Remote Control.

Use this setting to automate tasks that require interaction with other applications on the system, such as scripting or automation workflows.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable: point it at a marker file to suppress mobile push notifications while you're at the machine

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable allows you to specify a marker file that indicates your presence at a machine, which can be used to suppress mobile push notifications.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature matters because it enables you to avoid receiving redundant mobile push notifications when you're already actively working on a machine, reducing notification noise and potential distractions.
how_to_use: Set the CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE environment variable to point to a marker file on your machine, such as a hidden file in your home directory.
Ensure the marker file is updated or touched when you're actively using the machine, so that Claude Code can detect your presence and suppress mobile push notifications.

explanation.why_it_matters: This change reduces costs for developers who use web search or web fetch with API code execution, making it more economical to leverage these features in their applications.
how_to_use: Use web search to fetch data and then execute API code to process it without incurring extra costs
Combine web fetch with API code execution to retrieve and manipulate data from external sources at no additional charge

items.summary: The web search tool and programmatic tool calling are now generally available (no beta header required). Web search and web fetch now support dynamic filtering, which uses code execution to filter…

explanation.what_it_is: The web search tool and programmatic tool calling in the Anthropic API are now out of beta and available for general use, with added support for dynamic filtering using code execution.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows Claude Code users to leverage web search and web fetch with more precise control over the results, enabling more accurate and relevant data retrieval in their applications.
how_to_use: Use dynamic filtering to narrow down web search results based on custom criteria
Integrate web fetch with dynamic filtering to retrieve specific data from websites

items.summary: The code execution tool, web fetch tool, tool search tool, tool use examples, and memory tool are now generally available (no beta header required).

explanation.what_it_is: The code execution tool, web fetch tool, tool search tool, tool use examples, and memory tool are now fully available without beta restrictions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change means Claude Code users can rely on these tools for production use without worrying about beta limitations or potential changes to their functionality.
how_to_use: Use the code execution tool to run code snippets directly within Claude Code
Utilize the web fetch tool to fetch data from web APIs
Leverage the tool search tool to find and use relevant tools for specific tasks

items.summary: We've launched fast mode in research preview for Opus 4.6, providing significantly faster output token generation via the speed parameter. Fast mode is up to 2.5x as fast at premium pricing.…

explanation.what_it_is: Fast mode is a new feature in Opus 4.6 that generates output tokens up to 2.5x faster than the standard mode, accessible via the speed parameter.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to reduce the time spent on output token generation, enabling faster development and testing cycles, particularly for applications where speed is critical.
how_to_use: Set the speed parameter to enable fast mode in your Opus 4.6 requests
Test fast mode with premium pricing to evaluate its impact on your specific use case

items.summary: We've launched Claude Opus 4.6, our most intelligent model for complex agentic tasks and long-horizon work. Opus 4.6 recommends adaptive thinking (thinking: {type: "adaptive"}); manual thinking…

explanation.what_it_is: Claude Opus 4.6 is a model update that enables complex agentic tasks and long-horizon work, recommending adaptive thinking through the 'thinking' parameter with type set to 'adaptive'.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to tackle more intricate tasks that require flexible and dynamic thinking, potentially leading to more effective and efficient workflow outcomes.
how_to_use: Set the 'thinking' parameter to {type: 'adaptive'} to leverage adaptive thinking in your tasks
Use Opus 4.6 for tasks that require long-term planning and execution, such as complex project management or strategic decision-making

items.title: The effort parameter is now generally available (no beta header required) and…
items.summary: The effort parameter is now generally available (no beta header required) and supports Claude Opus 4.6. Effort replaces budget_tokens for controlling thinking depth on new models.

explanation.what_it_is: The effort parameter is a control for thinking depth in Claude models, replacing budget_tokens for new models, and is now supported in Claude Opus 4.6.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change allows for more precise control over the depth of thinking in Claude models, and simplifies the API by removing the need for beta headers and budget_tokens.
how_to_use: Use the effort parameter in place of budget_tokens when calling Claude models to control thinking depth.
Update existing API calls to remove beta headers for the effort parameter.

items.title: We've launched the compaction API in beta, providing server-side context…
items.summary: We've launched the compaction API in beta, providing server-side context summarization for effectively infinite conversations. Available on Opus 4.6.

explanation.what_it_is: The compaction API is a server-side context summarization tool that enables effective conversation handling beyond traditional limits.
explanation.why_it_matters: This API allows Claude Code users to handle conversations of virtually any length, making it particularly useful for applications requiring extensive dialogue management.
how_to_use: Use the compaction API to summarize conversation context on the server-side for applications built on Opus 4.6
Integrate the compaction API into chatbots or virtual assistants to improve their ability to understand and respond to long conversations

items.title: We've introduced data residency controls, allowing you to specify where model…
items.summary: We've introduced data residency controls, allowing you to specify where model inference runs with the inference_geo parameter. US-only inference is available at 1.1x pricing for models released after…

explanation.what_it_is: Data residency controls allow you to specify the geographic location where model inference runs using the inference_geo parameter.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables you to comply with data sovereignty requirements by controlling where your data is processed, with US-only inference available at a slightly higher pricing tier for newer models.
how_to_use: Use the inference_geo parameter to specify the desired geographic location for model inference, such as 'US' for US-only inference.
Check the pricing documentation for models released after the introduction of data residency controls to determine the 1.1x pricing tier for US-only inference.
